title: Bangladesh sends 90 more border guard platoons after arson on Awami League homes
dek: At least four people have died in political violence since 14 November as Sheikh Hasina says she will return from India in December. Fifty garment factories near Dhaka stayed shut.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Bangladesh deployed 90 more platoons of the paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) across the country on Saturday after a fresh wave of arson, including attacks on the homes of supporters of the banned Awami League, according to reports citing the state news agency. At least four people have been killed in political violence since 14 November, according to reports.

The deployment comes as former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who has lived in India since she was ousted in August 2024, says she will return to Bangladesh in December. She was sentenced to death in absentia last year for crimes against humanity over the crackdown on the 2024 protests.

## What happened

In the south-western district of Narail on Friday, more than a dozen homes linked to the Awami League were set on fire after the deaths of two activists of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) there, according to reports. One resident estimated that as many as 50 houses had been damaged, and roadblocks kept fire crews from reaching one site, reports said.

Earlier in the week, on Thursday, the Awami League's call for a nationwide "lockdown" to mark the anniversary of Ms Hasina's death sentence was followed by clashes and arson in several districts. Arsonists set fire to the ancestral home of Muhammad Yunus, the Nobel laureate who led the interim government after Ms Hasina's fall, in Chittagong, according to police as reported, and protesters targeted a police station in Gopalganj, her home district. On Thursday the BGB had already posted 96 to 97 platoons in seven districts including Dhaka and Chittagong; reports differ on the exact figure.

Reports differ on the toll. At least four people have died since 14 November, including three party activists and a bus worker, according to one count. Police reported 107 arrests after Thursday's violence, according to reports.

The national police chief, Md Ali Hossain Fakir, said security had been restored in Gopalganj, according to reports. Security was also reinforced in industrial areas.

## Garment belt stays tense

Separately, at least 50 garment factories stayed shut in the Savar and Ashulia industrial belt outside Dhaka on Saturday as workers kept up protests over minimum wages, according to reports. An Industrial Police superintendent said 11 factories had been closed under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act, which allows owners to shut a factory when workers stop work, and that others had declared holidays. The area was described as relatively calm, and factories were expected to reopen on Sunday. Talks in the wage board have stalled, as The Declaration reported this week.

## What the government says

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has accused the Awami League of conspiring against Bangladesh to please its "masters" across the border, an apparent reference to India. A minister has called Awami League activists a "terrorist group", according to reports. The Awami League, which called Thursday's lockdown to protest against Ms Hasina's sentence, had not responded publicly to the Narail arson by Saturday evening.

## Why it matters for India and Bengal

Ms Hasina's stay in India is the most sensitive issue between New Delhi and Dhaka. Bangladesh has asked India to extradite her; India has not done so. Any attempt by her to return from Indian soil in December would put India's handling of her stay under fresh scrutiny.

For West Bengal, which shares a 2,217 km border with Bangladesh, the unrest adds to strain on ties that are already showing up in daily life. Bangladesh's visa application centres in Kolkata and Siliguri will close after 30 November, and talks on renewing the Ganges water-sharing treaty, which expires in December, are taking place in Dhaka.

## What happens next

Ms Hasina has not given a date for her return. The Awami League has not announced its next protest programme, and the government has not said how long the extra BGB platoons will stay deployed.
